title: Respiratory & PAP Study Trail
description: Work through Steps 1 through 9 in order. Each step tells you what to learn first, where to apply it, when to take the 15-question checkpoint, and what topic comes next.
learnerBoundary: This trail supports RPSGT exam preparation. It does not replace physician orders, facility policy, scope requirements, manufacturer instructions, or current AASM/AAST authority.

steps.title: Recognize OSA and score the respiratory pattern
steps.whyThisMatters: Correct event recognition and scoring is the first branch point before treatment concepts make sense.
steps.primaryAuthority: AASM Scoring Manual Version 3 for adult respiratory scoring; ICSD-3-TR controls diagnostic classification.
steps.warning: Use AASM Version 3 for actual scoring rules. Do not use textbook wording or older scoring guidance to override current rules.

steps.title: Connect OSA findings to PAP treatment concepts
steps.whyThisMatters: The learner needs to separate adult OSA PAP treatment from CSA and ventilation-support pathways before choosing a response.
steps.primaryAuthority: AASM Adult PAP Treatment Guideline for adult OSA PAP treatment and support concepts.
steps.warning: This is the adult OSA PAP route. Do not generalize CPAP/APAP/BPAP treatment logic to CSA/ASV or hypoventilation/NIV.

steps.title: Apply the manual OSA titration pathway
steps.whyThisMatters: Manual CPAP/BPAP titration is a distinct technical workflow with its own treatment goal, response checks, and documentation needs.
steps.primaryAuthority: AASM manual PAP titration guidance with AAST PAP titration technical guidance; AASM Version 3 controls scoring.
steps.warning: Do not generalize OSA pressure-adjustment logic to ASV or NIV. Rule-sensitive scoring remains controlled by AASM Version 3.

steps.title: Troubleshoot comfort, interface, leak, and adherence barriers
steps.whyThisMatters: Many therapy failures are support problems rather than indications to change diagnosis or prescribe a different modality.
steps.primaryAuthority: AAST PAP acclimation/technical guidance and current scope/competency boundaries for technologist support.
steps.warning: Comfort, interface, education, and adherence support can cross PAP modalities; they do not decide diagnosis, treatment indication, modality, or device settings.

steps.title: Distinguish central and treatment-emergent events
steps.whyThisMatters: Central events change the reasoning pathway; they should be recognized and scored correctly before treatment decisions are considered.
steps.primaryAuthority: AASM Scoring Manual Version 3 for event scoring; ICSD-3-TR for classification; 2025 AASM CSA guidance for treatment.
steps.warning: Do not respond to central events by automatically applying the obstructive OSA pressure-increase pathway.

steps.title: Separate CSA treatment from advanced PAP/ASV concepts
steps.whyThisMatters: Advanced PAP belongs in a CSA-specific pathway, not as an extension of the routine OSA titration algorithm.
steps.primaryAuthority: 2025 AASM Adult Central Sleep Apnea Treatment Guideline.
steps.warning: The 2025 AASM CSA guideline controls current adult CSA treatment recommendations. Device-specific execution still requires the order, facility protocol, scope requirements, and manufacturer instructions.

steps.title: Recognize hypoventilation and keep NIV separate
steps.whyThisMatters: Ventilation support and CO2 monitoring answer a different clinical problem than routine obstructive PAP titration.
steps.primaryAuthority: AASM Version 3 for scoring plus current ETCO2/TcCO2 technical guidance; local orders and device instructions govern NIV execution.
steps.warning: Do not derive universal NIV settings, backup rates, target volumes, alarms, or pressure-support rules from OSA PAP or textbook material.

steps.title: Route oxygen with ventilation and CO2 in mind
steps.whyThisMatters: Oxygen can improve saturation without correcting the underlying respiratory event or inadequate ventilation.
steps.primaryAuthority: Pathway-dependent current AASM/AAST guidance plus the physician order, facility protocol, and applicable device instructions.
steps.warning: Improved SpO2 alone does not establish adequate ventilation. Keep ordered oxygen, OSA PAP titration oxygen, CSA, altitude, hypoventilation, and pediatric/infant routes distinct.

steps.title: Recognize, verify, document, correct, and escalate
steps.whyThisMatters: The technologist must distinguish a signal problem, a permitted technical correction, and a patient-safety issue that requires escalation.
steps.primaryAuthority: Current AAST role/scope guidance, AASM laboratory requirements, physician orders, and facility policy.
steps.warning: Use the sequence recognize → verify patient and signal → document → permitted technical correction → escalate per facility policy. If immediate patient danger is suspected, patient safety takes priority. Do not hard-code universal emergency or notification thresholds.
